name: Slide Atlas
description: Pathology operations proposal with floating glass, specimen lineage and editable laboratory infographics.

slides.title: SLIDE
items:
Pathology operations
From specimen to signed report

slides.title: The specimen carries a chain of evidence
items: A complete report depends on a traceable route through the laboratory. Every transfer must preserve the link to the original request.
The specimen, request and laboratory identifier remain connected.
Blocks and slides retain their relationship to the parent case.
The authorized report returns through the agreed clinical channel.

slides.title: One case can create several tracked objects
items: Illustrative lineage of one case, two blocks and six slides. Local preparation determines the actual number of objects.

slides.title: Preparation makes the material readable
items: The laboratory records the work performed on each case and links the resulting slides to the reporting record.
Conceptual laboratory illustration. The tissue artwork has no diagnostic meaning.

slides.title: The route from receipt to authorization
items: Reconcile the specimen and request. Record discrepancies through the local process.
Create and track the required blocks and slides under the approved laboratory procedure.
The reporting professional reviews the prepared material and requests further work when needed.
The report reaches the requesting team with its identity and status intact.

slides.title: The queue has several kinds of work
items: The coordinator reviews the stage of each case before assigning capacity. Cases awaiting information remain visible in the same review.

slides.title: Turnaround has several components
items: Illustrative median stage intervals, working days
These stage medians describe separate distributions. The end-to-end median must be measured directly from case timestamps.

slides.title: Exceptions need a visible return path
items: The reviewer checks the material and information required for the report.
The request records the responsible team and the next review point.

slides.title: Workload changes with the case mix
items: Synthetic weekly case counts by local workload group
A count of cases alone cannot describe reporting effort. Review the local workload mix alongside staff availability and open exceptions.
Groups A and B are fictional planning categories.

slides.title: Quality measures keep the handovers visible
items: Cases with a complete receipt record in the synthetic audit.
Authorized reports with a recorded destination in the synthetic audit.
The pilot also records corrections and repeat work so throughput gains can be reviewed with quality.

slides.title: The case record connects five roles
A staged rollout protects traceability
items: Test the relationship between case, block, slide and report in sample records.
Review every exception and correction with the staff who handle the handover.

slides.title: The pilot has a £240k planning envelope
items: Backfill and supervised training during the pilot.
Identifier mapping and the interfaces needed for the case record.
Audit time, issue resolution and rollout coordination.
Illustrative budget for service planning; actual procurement and staffing costs require local estimates.

slides.title: A clear record behind every report
items: The pilot decision rests on traceability, workload and the quality of each handover.
The proposed review joins open-case counts, stage intervals, correction records and staff feedback before another laboratory section joins.
Fictional laboratory and synthetic data. All laboratory images are conceptual AI artwork, with no diagnostic interpretation.
